newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BILL ON TAX EXEMPTIONS GOES TO PARLIAMENT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BILL ON TAX EXEMPTIONS GOES TO PARLIAMENT.

text.p: The Greek draft bill on tax exemptions , one of the main pillars of 1997 budget, was submitted to parliament today, parliament officials told Reuters.
Investors will pre-pay a 7.5 percent tax on interest from T-bills issued from January 1 but the state will withhold the same tax at maturity for renewed T-bills, said the draft bill.
"The tax liability for these incomes is exhausted with this pre-collection or withholding tax," it said.
The 7.5 percent tax on bonds is withheld by the persons authorised by the Bank of Greece when coupons are redeemed, it said.
The tax applies to both physical and book-entry securities.
Bonds issued by the EIB, EBRD, IFC and other international organisations in Greece will be subject to the 7.5 percent tax starting January 1, it said.
Interest from T-bills and bonds issued by December 31, 1996 will not be subject to the 7.5 percent tax.
Investment companies will have to pay a 0.2 percent tax annually that is calculated on their average investments plus reserves at current prices as appearing on their quarterly investment tables.
The tax has to be paid in the first half of July and January following the calculation period.
The dividends distributed to the shareholders of investment companies will not be subject to an income tax.
The 0.02 percent tax also applies to the six-month average of net assets of mutual funds.
Investment companies will be able to pay this tax on incomes earned from July 1, 1994 to December 31, 1995 and mutual funds for the period July 1, 1994 to June 30, 1996, it said.
The draft bill does not mention anything about taxes on derivatives. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
